slides.title: Fill your moka pot without the guesswork
slides.subtitle: Water, coffee, flame: three habits for your stovetop moka.

slides.myth: Press the coffee down firmly, like you would for espresso.
slides.truth: Fill the basket generously, but don't press. Water needs an easy path through the grounds. Just level the top with your finger.

slides.title: Fill it in this order
steps: Pour cold water up to the safety valve's lower edge.
Fill the basket generously with ground coffee. Don't press.
Level the top with a finger and wipe the rim.
Close the pot firmly and set it on low heat.

slides.title: Why stop below the valve
slides.body: The valve is there for safety. Keep the water at its lower edge so the valve stays free to do its job.

slides.label: The tip
slides.body: Set the flame to low and give it time. Great moka coffee is worth the wait.

slides.title: Water, coffee, flame: in that order
slides.body: Three habits, no extra gear. Your moka does the rest.
